newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - NOV 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - NOV 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government bows to the powerful and is merciless with the weak: the abolition of tax breaks will proceed more gradually than originally conceived but large families will get a welfare cut of 80 billion drachmas.

--Industrial action is expected to intensify in the wake of the announcement yesterday of the government's economic measures. Workers in the public and private sectors will strike for 24 hours tomorrow.

--Former prime minister and honorary president of the main opposition party New Democracy Constantine Mitsotakis yesterday chose to play hard ball, accusing his successor as ND leader, Miltiades Evert, of trying to "conquer" the party and claiming that the party "no longer operates democratically".
--Yesterday's attack from Mitsotakis was a fatal blow to the conservative opposition party's unity: the continuation of the saga is expected at today's critical Political Council meeting.

--The long hand of the government reaches deep into the pockets of all: large families, bonuses and scooters - which now have to pay registration fees - all come under the government spotlight. The abolition of some 200 plus tax breaks will bring the government 130 billion drachmas.

--Constantine Karamanlis, former president and founder of New Democracy, adds his voice to the cacophony in ND. Leader hopeful George Souflias attempts to distance himself from Mitsotakis's statements yesterday.
--Municipal charges in Athens will go up by 8.3 percent.
--Welfare benefits to 208,000 large families are cut while 46 sparsely-occupied islands become 'tax havens' under a programme of incentives for growth.

--The ongoing crisis in New Democracy has thrown a lifebelt to Prime Minister Costas Simitis. As workers rise up in protest at the government's new measures, the main opposition party finds itself unable to extricate itself from its internal squabbles and rise to the occasion. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
